title: Prototype 'Pathfinder': per-request kernel advisor using architecture + sequence-length fingerprints
creator: Avery Chen
description: We need a lightweight, per-request advisory layer ('Pathfinder') that suggests the best kernel implementation pair (prefill kernel + decode kernel) given a request fingerprint. The goal is to reduce tail latency and cost regressions by making kernel selection decisions that account for hardware family, token sequence-length distribution, and recent thermal/occupancy signals without adding significant scheduling overhead. Pathfinder is not a replacement for the runtime's global autotuner; it's a low-latency recommendation service that combines cached microbenchmarks, a compact cost model, and a short Monte Carlo probe policy to choose kernels per request or per-request-class.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible prototype binary that receives a request fingerprint and returns a recommended (prefill_kernel, decode_kernel) tuple in <200us median added latency
Prototype integrates with the runtime probe harness and can run A/B traffic split against the existing heuristic router

Observed cost/latency improvement >= 5% p50 latency or >= 8% token-cost reduction in at least one internal production-like workload (web & assistant workloads), with no >3% regressions on other workloads
Test harness for cold-cache and hot-cache scenarios with mocked occupancy and thermal signals
Design doc and experiment plan reviewed by runtime and infra teams; at least two peer review approvals on the initial PR
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after spike session with runtime team; outlined goals and constraints (must be <200us overhead, resilient to model rollouts)

2025-02-18: Collected candidate features for fingerprinting: architecture family tag, scheduled GPU memory usage, sequence_length_bucket (0-16,17-64,65-256,256+), recent KV cache hit rate, model variant tag. Agreed to keep fingerprint <= 128 bits.
2025-02-22: Implemented microbenchmark cache schema and in-memory LRU with TTL; measured 350ns median lookup in prototype harness (Go).

2025-02-25: First cost model implemented: linear regression over (seq_len, batch_size, kernel_choice) using recent microbenchmark samples + regularization. Produced reasonable estimates in synthetic matrix tests.

2025-02-28: Ran closed beta experiment on staging: Pathfinder recommended a non-default decode kernel for 12% of requests; p50 improved by 6% for long-sequence jobs, tail unaffected. Need deeper analysis on short-sequence churn.

2025-03-04: Incorporated Monte Carlo probe policy to occasionally test alternate kernel choices (~1% of requests) and log outcomes for online re-calibration. Preparing PR for runtime integration; adding dashboards for per-kernel regret and probe outcomes.
decisions: Compact fingerprint chosen: (hw_family, seq_bucket, model_tag, kv_hit_bin, batch_bin) — balances discriminative power and storage overhead
Use an in-memory microbenchmark cache with TTL and LRU eviction rather than persistent store for first pass to minimize I/O; persistent aggregation can be added later
Hybrid selection policy: cost-model rank with epsilon-greedy probing for exploration (epsilon default 0.01). This is simpler than a full bandit controller and easier to audit for regressions
Keep admission control: Pathfinder will only override runtime default when expected latency or cost improvement exceeds calibrated thresholds to reduce flapping
tradeoffs: Per-request advisor reduces global autotuner visibility into aggregated stats; mitigate by logging probe outcomes to the global telemetry pipeline and periodically re-training global autotuner
Compact fingerprint reduces dimensionality but may conflate edge cases (rare models + rare sequence lengths). We'll detect by looking for high-regret fingerprints and fall back to safe defaults
Epsilon-greedy probing is conservative and simpler than Thompson sampling; we prioritize safety & explainability for early rollout
related_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4728 -- prototype branch and microbenchmark cache implementation
qa_plan: Unit tests covering fingerprint canonicalization, TTL eviction, and cost-model training step
Integration test with runtime probe harness to validate <200us added latency on representative hardware (A100, H100, T4)
Staging A/B (10% traffic) for 72 hours with automatic roll-back if tail latency > 3% or errors spike > 0.5%
Chaos test: simulate microbenchmark staleness by advancing system clock and ensure fallbacks behave correctly
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Canary deploy on non-production staging pools, validate metrics and dashboards
Stage 1: 1% production traffic with probe-only mode (recommendations logged but not applied)
Stage 2: 5% traffic, apply recommendations for low-risk fingerprints (long sequences on H100 family)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% while monitoring per-workload regressions; full rollout gated on success criteria
metrics: p50 / p95 / p99 latency delta (ms) per-workload
probe regret (difference between chosen kernel latency and best observed)
recommendation coverage (fraction of requests receiving non-default recommendation)
recommendation stability (fraction of fingerprints that flip recommended kernel week-over-week)
notes: Next: finalize PR and get design doc review from Runtime Leads (A. Singh, R. Patel).
Follow-up: plan for automated fingerprint retirement when regret consistently exceeds threshold; propose as follow-on in runtime-autotune roadmap.
